haiku-low.q1: In step 4, after step 3 passes and before any new-release instance starts, one migrate task runs. The live colour, still on the old release, must keep working on the migrated schema, since migrations are additive.
haiku-low.q2: Only after the release still using the old column or table has been retired, in step 11 of the deploy that replaced it.
haiku-low.q3: All 4 new instances must pass 3 consecutive /healthz checks, then smoke tests must pass, before gate_deadline (10 minutes after step 5). If not, Abort: scale the new colour to 0 and leave the listener alone.
haiku-low.q4: In step 8, the public listener is repointed from the old target group to the new one in a single change. New requests go to the new colour; in-flight requests on the old colour finish.
haiku-low.q5: The 5xx rate on the public listener exceeding 1% over a rolling 5-minute window, between T and T+15, or an engineer starting the rollback job from T onward. Rollback repoints the listener to the old colour, scales the new colour to 0, and alerts the team. It never reverses migrations and leaves the old colour unchanged.
haiku-low.q6: Until step 11, at T+30 minutes after switched_at. Problems found during the hold are handled by an engineer starting the rollback job. After T+30 there is no fast switch back; rollback means a normal deploy of the previous release.
haiku-low.q7: A failed transaction rolls back, leaving the schema unchanged. A failed index build has its invalid index dropped, while committed table and column changes stay and the index reruns next deploy. The run stops, the new colour never starts, the live colour keeps serving, and the run goes to step 12 (failed).
haiku-low.q8: In step 2, the run reads which target group the public listener forwards to; that colour is live and the other is new. The listener is the only lasting record. live_colour and new_colour are run variables kept only for the run.
haiku-low.q9: A CI concurrency group (for example deploy-catalog-web) makes later runs queue while one run holds it. The run keeps it until step 12, when it finishes and releases the group.
haiku-low.q10: Step 5 points an internal test listener, reachable only from CI (for example port 8443), at the new target group. The smoke suite runs through it while the public listener keeps users on the live colour.
haiku-low.q11: The pipeline runs one migrate task from the new image. Instances never migrate on startup, so migrations run exactly once per deploy.
haiku-low.q12: After an abort or rollback, the new colour is scaled to 0. If that scale-down fails on abort, the team is alerted. The next deploy's step 2 scales the new colour to 0 if needed, and it deploys into that colour.

sonnet.q1: Step 4, after build/check (step 3) and before the new colour starts (step 5). The live colour (old release) must keep working on the migrated schema, since all migrations are additive.
sonnet.q2: Only in a later release, after the release that still used the old column/table has been retired (in step 11 of the deploy that replaced it).
sonnet.q3: All 4 new instances must each pass 3 consecutive /healthz checks (step 6), then the smoke suite must pass (step 7), all before gate_deadline (start of step 5 + 10 min). If not in time, Abort: scale new colour to 0, leave public listener alone, go to step 12 (failed).
sonnet.q4: Step 8: the public listener is repointed from the old target group to the new one in a single change; new requests go to the new colour, while the old colour keeps running so in-flight requests finish.
sonnet.q5: Automatic rollback is triggered when the public listener's 5xx rate (rolling 5-min window) exceeds 1% during T to T+15 min. An engineer can also start the pipeline's rollback job (from T on, including during hold). Rollback repoints the public listener to the old colour's target group, scales new colour to 0 and alerts the team. It never reverses migrations (they stay applied).
sonnet.q6: Until step 11 at T+30 min (old colour is scaled to 0 then). Automatic watch covers T to T+15; during hold (T+15 to T+30) an engineer starts the rollback job. After T+30 there is no fast switch back; rolling back means a normal deploy of the previous release through this checklist.
sonnet.q7: If the table/column transaction fails, it rolls back and the schema is unchanged. If an index build fails, the invalid index is dropped; the committed table/column changes stay (safe, additive) and the unrecorded index migration reruns in the next deploy. Either way the deploy stops: new colour never started, live colour keeps serving, go to step 12 (failed).
sonnet.q8: Step 2 reads which target group the public listener forwards to: that is the live colour, the other is the new colour. The load balancer's public listener is the only lasting record (no state file); the run also writes live_colour and new_colour to pipeline run variables for the life of the run.
sonnet.q9: A CI concurrency group (e.g. deploy-catalog-web); one run holds it and later runs queue. The run keeps the slot from step 1 until step 12 (Finish), including through rollback until the listener is back on the old colour.
sonnet.q10: Through an internal test listener (reachable only from CI, e.g. port 8443) pointed at the new colour's target group, while the public listener still forwards to the live colour.
sonnet.q11: A single `migrate` task run by the pipeline from the new image against the shared database in step 4. Instances never migrate on startup, so migrations run exactly once per deploy (and only pending ones, per the migration history table).
sonnet.q12: Both abort and rollback scale the new colour to 0 (idle and empty). If that scale-down fails, the team is alerted and step 2 of the next deploy scales that colour to 0 before using it. (Also: the colour left with 0 instances is the one the next run deploys into.)
